- Assessed Russian Advances

Shading under the following layers will not qualify:
- Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas
- Claimed Russian Territory

The count fell from 550,000 to 410,000 in one week, organizers are shifting to sit-ins rather than marches, routes are being kept out of city centres, and the union general strike is set for Nov 5, not Oct 31. Interior Minister Nuñez expects a large turnout, so a rebound cannot be ruled out, but a rise of about 90,000 over the previous Saturday is a stretch.

questions.question: 🇫🇷🪧 Will France report 500,000+ protesters on at least 1 of the next 2 Saturdays (Oct 24 or Oct 31, 2026)?
questions.resolution_criteria: Context: the first big "vie chere" protest day, on Saturday Oct 17, 2026, drew 550,000 protesters according to the French Ministry of the Interior (800,000 according to organizers). Resolves YES if the Ministry of the Interior (or, if it publishes no national figure, police figures reported by AFP) reports more than 500,000 protesters nationwide on Saturday Oct 24, 2026 or on Saturday Oct 31, 2026 (at least one of the two), in protests against the cost of living (vie chere) or the related social movement. Organizers' or unions' figures do not count. The Oct 17 day does not count. Resolves NO otherwise, including if no protest takes place. The market closes before the first of these figures is public.

forecasts.rationale: Democrats start from about 214-215 seats and need 236 or more, a net gain of about 21. Cook's Oct 23 ratings have 220 seats Solid/Likely/Lean Democratic, 198 Republican and 17 toss-ups with a projected Democratic gain of 12-22 seats, while generic-ballot leads of 8-9 points (Marist, Ipsos) are close to 2018's, which produced exactly 235. Waves tend to break toward the winning party and the maps changed since 2018, so the threshold sits near the middle of the plausible range; I put it slightly below even.

questions.question: Will the Democrats Outperform their 2018 Midterm Results? [Win more than 235 seats in 2026]

forecasts.rationale: Republicans won the last three Florida Senate races (2018 by 0.2 points, 2022 by 16, 2024 by 13), Florida's Republican registration edge is about 1.55 million, and appointed incumbent Moody led by 4 in a University of North Florida poll of Oct 21. Democrat Nixon out-raised Moody from July 30 to Sept 30 and the national environment favours Democrats, so the race is closer than 2022 and 2024, but a win would need a larger swing than one poll shows. A third candidate, Gillespie, is also on the ballot.
